sections.changelog:
Added

  • **Automatic search-statistics cleanup.** A daily background sweep now trims the search-log and click tables, dropping rows untouched for a configurable retention window (new "Keep search statistics for N days" field on the Index tab, default 90; 0 keeps everything). Actively searched phrases never age out, so the analytics — and the click table joined into ranking when click-boost is on — stop growing without bound.
  • **Live-search error feedback.** When a request fails (network error or a non-OK response), the dropdown now shows a localized "could not load results" message instead of silently leaving an empty panel and a stuck spinner.

Changed

  • **Category suggestions in the dropdown follow the distinctive part of the query.** When a search combines catalogue-wide words shared by every category (a phone model like "iPhone 12 Pro") with a defining word ("battery"), the category list no longer fills up with unrelated categories that merely matched the model words. A category is now suggested only when its products match the query as fully as the best-matching product does, so a battery search surfaces the battery category rather than cases and glass too. Broad queries with no defining word still list every relevant category.
  • **"Balanced" strictness now actually relaxes on short queries.** The default coverage floor was equal to "strict" for two- and three-word queries (the most common case). It now drops about one concept per three words (a three-word query matches on two of three), giving real recall for balanced mode while keeping two-word queries strict.
  • **Incremental catch-up defaults to once a day for new installs.** The safety-net sweep scans `post_modified_gmt`, a column WordPress core does not index, so an hourly default was needlessly heavy on large catalogs. Existing sites keep their chosen interval.
  • **Index schema upgraded to v7.** The index table gains a unique row key and a covering key for the ranking query. Because the index is derived from your content, the upgrade rebuilds it cleanly in the background (the fresh table gets the new keys instantly) instead of rewriting a large live table in place — the site stays responsive throughout, and search fills back in within a few minutes.

Fixed

  • **Index integrity under concurrent writes.** A missing unique constraint let a race between the save hook, the cron catch-up and a manual reindex insert duplicate rows that doubled a product's ranking score; writes are now idempotent, serialized per object with a MySQL advisory lock, and the term-frequency statistics can no longer be double-counted.
  • **Catch-up no longer skips edits made during an empty pass.** The watermark is left on the last processed row instead of jumping to "now", closing a small window where an external write could slip below the cursor and be missed.
  • **Mobile full-screen overlay is more robust.** A stale response for a just-cleared query can no longer reopen the panel; rotating the device or crossing the mobile breakpoint closes an open overlay instead of leaving the page scroll-locked; tabbing out of the widget closes it; and the body scroll lock is reference-counted so one search form closing no longer unlocks the page under another that is still open.
  • **Keyboard and screen-reader access to the dropdown.** Category and brand suggestions are now reachable with the arrow keys, the announced result count matches what is actually rendered (including per-group caps), and switching result tabs no longer leaves the active-descendant pointing at a hidden option.

Performance

  • **Fewer repeated queries and rebuilds per search.** The dropdown's category/brand coverage aggregate is computed once per request instead of once for categories and again for brands; the synonym map and query-term expansion are memoized per request instead of being rebuilt on every run, retry and facet pass; and the covering index removes per-row bookmark lookups from the main ranking query.

Removed

  • **Price interpretation in the search box.** Numbers typed into search are treated purely as model/spec identifiers, never as a price range — a query such as "1660-2060" or "8-800-555" is searched as text and is no longer turned into a price filter. The natural-language price parser and its "Understand price in the query" toggle have been removed. Explicit price controls on the results page (the price-range facet and price sorting) are unaffected.
  • **Unused ranking settings.** `boost_recency` and `candidate_pool_cap` were declared and sanitized but never read; they have been removed.
